# Load data

```{r, auxillary.model.information}

# Since the data falls within two UTM zones and there is not an ideal projection to use, apply a custom equal area Albers projection
aea_custom <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=30 +lat_2=50 +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-124.5 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

# High res coastal boundary from NOAA
land.barrier <- read_sf(here("Data", "Shapefiles",
                             "land.barrier.shp"))

# Load YearSeason gaps to fill
load(file = here("Data", "ExampleRun",
                 "est.missing.time2.rda"))

```

# Create plot graticule labels

Note this is only for graph labels and is chosen based on the mean lat and lon values of the haul transect locations.

```{r, Create.plot.label.breaks}

lat_breaks <- seq(27, 55, 4)  # Latitude breaks

lat_labels <- c(paste(27, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(31, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(35, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(39, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(43, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(47, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(51, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(55, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""))

```

# Create base map

Note that cropping should be done before projecting the data and projecting the data should be done before any intersection analysis.

```{r, basemap}

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Make coastline backdrop
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

PacificCoast <- ne_countries(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf") 
PacificCoast.wgs84 <- st_crop(PacificCoast, xmin = -133, xmax = -110, 
                               ymin = 25, ymax = 55)
class(PacificCoast)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot output
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.wgs84, fill = "#D2B48C", col = "#927143") +
    xlab("Longitude") + ylab("Latitude") +
    ggtitle("West Coast map") +
    theme_classic()

```

## Apply min and max geographical extents

```{r, adjust.map.dimensions}

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Find spatial extents
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

xmin <- st_bbox(PacificCoast.wgs84)["xmin"]
xmin
# [1] -133

xmax <- st_bbox(PacificCoast.wgs84)["xmax"]
xmax
# [1] -110
  
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

PacificCoast.wgs84.map <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.wgs84,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          size = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  theme_void() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(27,55), 
                     breaks = lat_breaks, 
                     labels = lat_labels, 
                     expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
  labs(y = "Latitude")

PacificCoast.wgs84.map

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a mapping boundary box
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

pacific_bbox <- st_bbox(PacificCoast.wgs84)
#     xmin ymin xmax ymax
# [1] -133   27 -111   55

```

## Create hline boundaries

Because the current model looks at only the Northern sub population in US waters, one of the boundary extents should include the national boarders. The second should look at the coast of California where the most mixing is thought to occur for Pacific Sardine sub populations (under the current survey hypothesis). From the data we are looking at data from UTM zone 10 and UTM zone 11. However, using the USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic project (ESRI:102003) skews Canadian and Mexican data extents. The therefore the use of aea_custom was chosen.

```{r, find.original.model.break.dimensions}

# First transform the data to be able to do intersection analysis
PacificCoast.aea_custom <- st_transform(PacificCoast.wgs84, 
                                        crs = aea_custom)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In order to find the state boundary extents, use ne_states function in 
# rnaturalearth
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Find state boundaries
PCoastStates.wgs84 <- ne_states(returnclass = "sf")

PCoastStates.aea_custom <-
  # Convert to m for intersection
  st_transform(PCoastStates.wgs84, crs = aea_custom) 

PCoastStates.aea_custom <- 
  st_intersection(PCoastStates.aea_custom, PacificCoast.aea_custom)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In order to find the state boundary extents, use ne_states function in 
# rnaturalearth
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Find state boundaries
PCoastStates.wgs84 <- ne_states(returnclass = "sf")

PCoastStates.aea_custom <-
  # transform to NAD83 / Conus Albers
  st_transform(PCoastStates.wgs84, crs = aea_custom) 

PCoastStates.aea_custom <- st_intersection(PCoastStates.aea_custom,
                                           PacificCoast.aea_custom)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# populated areas (cities and city names)
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

Populated10.wgs84 <- ne_download(scale = 110, 
                                 type = "populated_places_simple", 
                                 category = "cultural", 
                                 returnclass = "sf") 

Populated10.aea_custom <- Populated10.wgs84 %>%
  st_transform(., crs = aea_custom)

Populated10.aea_custom <- st_intersection(Populated10.aea_custom,
                                          PCoastStates.aea_custom)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For EEZ definitions 
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note: Because you are cropping to study extent you need to put disclaimer!
## Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) boundaries are filled by region and 
## clipped to the study extent (27°N–55°N, 111°W–133°W) without explicit 
## boundary lines for cartographic clarity. Displayed spatial extents are for 
## analytical reference and do not imply official political endorsement or 
## territorial adjudication.

# For the U.S.
# Download US EEZ polygons directly from MarineRegions.org
us_eez_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'United States' OR sovereign2 = 'United States'")
us_eez <- us_eez_raw %>% 
  # Crop the polygon to the Pacific region
  st_crop(pacific_bbox) %>%
  # Transform to your custom projection AFTER cropping
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom) %>% 
  # Clean up any geometry artifacts along the crop edge
  st_make_valid()

# For Canada
canada_eez_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'Canada' OR sovereign2 = 'Canada'")
canada_eez <- canada_eez_raw %>% 
  # Crop the polygon to the Pacific region
  st_crop(pacific_bbox) %>%
  # Transform to your custom projection AFTER cropping
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom) %>% 
  # Clean up any geometry artifacts along the crop edge
  st_make_valid()

# For Overlapping claims
contested_cad_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'Canada' OR sovereign2 = 'Canada'") %>% 
  filter(pol_type == "Overlapping claim") 
dim(contested_cad_raw)
# [1] 1 32

# For Mexico
mexico_eez_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'Mexico' OR sovereign2 = 'Mexico'")
mexico_eez <- mexico_eez_raw %>% 
  # Crop the polygon to the Pacific region
  st_crop(pacific_bbox) %>%
  # Transform to your custom projection AFTER cropping
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom) %>% 
  # Clean up any geometry artifacts along the crop edge
  st_make_valid()

#------------------------------
# Check For Overlapping claims
#------------------------------

## For U.S.
contested_us_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'United States' OR sovereign2 = 'United States'") %>% 
  filter(pol_type == "Overlapping claim") %>% 
  # Crop the polygon to the Pacific region
  st_crop(pacific_bbox) 
dim(contested_us_raw)
# [1] 0 32

## For Canada
contested_cad_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'Canada' OR sovereign2 = 'Canada'") %>% 
  filter(pol_type == "Overlapping claim") %>% 
  # Crop the polygon to the Pacific region
  st_crop(pacific_bbox) 
dim(contested_cad_raw)
# [1] 0 32

## For Mexico
contested_mex_raw <- mrp_get("eez", cql_filter = "sovereign1 = 'Mexico' OR sovereign2 = 'Mexico'") %>% 
  filter(pol_type == "Overlapping claim") %>% 
  # Crop the polygon to the Pacific region
  st_crop(pacific_bbox) 
dim(contested_mex_raw)
# [1] 0 32

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Put everything together for the polygons
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Extract pure geometries
geom_us     <- st_geometry(us_eez)
geom_canada <- st_geometry(canada_eez)
geom_mexico <- st_geometry(mexico_eez)

# 2. Build individual sf objects
us_clean     <- st_sf(Region = "Pacific U.S. EEZ", geometry = geom_us)
canada_clean <- st_sf(Region = "Pacific Canadian EEZ", geometry = geom_canada)
mexico_clean <- st_sf(Region = "Pacific Mexican EEZ", geometry = geom_mexico)

# 3. Combine all active non-empty regions into one dataset
eez_zones <- bind_rows(
  us_clean, 
  canada_clean, 
  mexico_clean
)

# Plot using color fill based on Region
plot(eez_zones["Region"])

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a transformed line for residual plots
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Create northern stock boundary (Westernmost Point, CA)
nstock <- st_sf(
  geometry = 
    st_sfc(
      st_linestring(matrix(c(-133, 40.4385, -111, 40.4385), 
                           ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))),
  crs = 4326
  ) %>%
  st_transform(., crs = aea_custom)

# Create southern stock boundary (Point Conception, CA)
point.concept <- st_sf(
  geometry = 
    st_sfc(
      st_linestring(matrix(c(-133, 34.4486, -111, 34.4486), 
                           ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))),
  crs = 4326
  ) %>%
  st_transform(., crs = aea_custom)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = nstock, col = "blue", 
             linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_sf(data = point.concept, col = "red", 
             linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "longdash") +# 1. EEZ 4-Zone Layer
  geom_sf(data = eez_zones,
          color = NA,
          alpha = 0.5,
          aes(fill = Region)) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "EEZ Region",
    values = c(
      "Pacific Canadian EEZ"      = "lightblue",
      "Pacific U.S. EEZ"          = "lightgreen",
      "Pacific Mexican EEZ"       = "yellowgreen"
    )
  ) +
  
  # 2. Land Layers
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = Populated10.aea_custom) +
  geom_sf_text(data = Populated10.aea_custom,
               aes(label = name), 
               nudge_y = 50000,  # Offset text 40km north so it doesn't overlap the point
               size = 3.5,
               fontface = "bold"
               ) +
  # Remove added space on x-axis
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0))

```

# Plot initial patterns

```{r, inital.plots}

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For All Data
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

AllYears.dat <- fread(here("Data",
                           "AllYears.Unfiltered.Canada.and.CPS.ATM.Survey.Data.csv"))

AllYears.dat_aea <- AllYears.dat %>%
  mutate(FID = keys) %>%
  make_transect_sf(., crs = 4326) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  st_transform(., aea_custom) 

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For U.S. Spring Data
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

USSpring.dat_aea <- AllYears.dat_aea %>% 
  # Note the Spring survey was exclusive conducted by the U.S.,
  # but I keep the filter here to remain consistent.
  filter(Season == "Spring" & Country == "USA") %>% 
  st_centroid() %>% 
  mutate(
    log_haul = log(Haul.kg.m3),
    is_absent = is.infinite(log_haul) | is.na(log_haul)
  )

# Plot spatial density for spring
## Note absences are Inf so colored grey 
us.spring.dat <- ggplot() +
  # 1. Add EEZ boundaries
  geom_sf(data = eez_zones,
          color = NA,
          alpha = 0.5,
          aes(fill = Region)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "EEZ Region",
    values = c(
      "Pacific Canadian EEZ"      = "lightblue",
      "Pacific U.S. EEZ"          = "lightgreen",
      "Pacific Mexican EEZ"       = "yellowgreen"
    )
  ) +
  # 2. Land Layers
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  ## Remove added space on x-axis
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  # 3. ABSENCE points (log = -Inf or 0 kg/m3) mapped to a manual aesthetic
  geom_sf(data = filter(USSpring.dat_aea, is_absent),
          aes(shape = "Absent from Haul"), 
          color = "grey", 
          size = 1.5) +
  # 4. PRESENCE points mapped to the continuous color scale
  geom_sf(data = filter(USSpring.dat_aea, !is_absent),
          aes(color = log_haul), 
          size = 1.5) +
  # 5. Continuous Color Bar
  scale_colour_gradient2(
    name = "log(Haul kg/m³)",
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red",
    midpoint = 0
  ) +
  # 6. Discrete Shape Legend for Absent
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Status",
    values = c("Absent from Haul" = 16) # 16 is a solid point circle
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 6) +
  labs(y = "Latitude") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        panel.spacing = unit(2, "pt"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 0, r = 2, b = 0, l = 2, unit = "pt")
  )

us.spring.dat

ggsave2(filename="US.survey.data.spring.distribution.jpeg",
        plot=us.spring.dat, 
        device = "jpeg", 
        path = here("Final.Figures"),
        dpi = 1200, 
        width = 45,      # Expanded width to accommodate two side-by-side multi-facet maps
        height = 21, 
        units = "cm", 
        limitsize = FALSE
)
```

# Load base model data (historic) and restructure

```{r, load.final.model.and.cleaned.data}

# Load grouped length data
data_for_3bin_model <- fread(here("Data", "data_for_3bin_model_w_zeros.csv"),
                             sep = ",")

# Filter group length data to include 200 mm cutoff
TwoLenBin200.dat <- data_for_3bin_model %>%
  select(-c(len.bin, merged.bin2)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(merged.bin = as.factor(merged.bin)) %>%
  mutate(merged.bin =
           case_when(merged.bin == "less200" ~ "less 20.0 cm",
                     merged.bin == "200plus" ~ "20.0+ cm"))

# Load global mesh
barrier2mld_42.5 <- readRDS(
  file = here(dir, "Final.Results",
              "barrier2mld_42.5.rds"))

# Refit mesh to filtered group length data
TwoLenBin200Mesh <- sdmTMB::make_mesh(
  data = TwoLenBin200.dat, 
  xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), 
  mesh = barrier2mld_42.5$mesh # This "borrows" the physical structure of the old mesh
)

# Re-run best model
deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB(
  Total_W ~ 0 + as.factor(Year) + merged.bin,
  data = TwoLenBin200.dat, 
  family = delta_lognormal(type = "standard"),
  mesh = TwoLenBin200Mesh,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = "YearSeas.nm",
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  spatial = "on",
  spatial_varying = ~ merged.bin,
  anisotropy = FALSE,
  reml = TRUE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use
  offset = "LogArea",
  #fold_ids = "fold_id",
  silent = TRUE
)

sanity(deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml)
# ✔ Non-linear minimizer suggests successful convergence
# ✔ Hessian matrix is positive definite
# ✔ No extreme or very small eigenvalues detected
# ✔ No gradients with respect to fixed effects are >= 0.001
# ✔ No fixed-effect standard errors are NA
# ✔ No standard errors look unreasonably large
# ✔ No sigma parameters are < 0.01
# ✔ No sigma parameters are > 100
# ✔ Range parameters don't look unreasonably large

# Clear un-used memory
gc()

```

# Explore model outputs

DHARMa is designed to check overall model assumptions for GLMMs, while mle-mvn specifically checks consistency with a multivariate normal distribution of observations. 

If DHARMa looks great but mle-mvn looks terrible, it usually means your observation  model (the family and link function) is fine, but your random effects structure (spatial fields or intercepts) might be problematic.

mle-mvn is simulation-based. If you run that exact line of code twice, you will get slightly different numbers both times. To make your plots reproducible, it is good practice to wrap it in a seed.


# Create a 10 km x 10 km grid

```{r, create grid}

# Expand bounding box by 50 m each side and convert to polygon in one step
bbox <- st_bbox(TwoLenBin200.dat.sf) + c(-50, -50, 50, 50)

bbox_poly <- st_as_sfc(bbox, crs = st_crs(TwoLenBin200.dat.sf))

# Create grid
grid <- st_make_grid(
  bbox_poly,
  # corresponds to a 10km x 10km grid
  cellsize = c(10000, 10000),
  what = "centers"
) 

# Save as sf object
grid_vect <- vect(grid)

# Convert to raster
grid_rast <- rast(grid_vect, resolution = 10000)

# Assign values to the grid cells
values(grid_rast) <- 1:ncell(grid_rast) 

```

# Join ROMS data by spatial and temporal step

```{r, structure.data}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Identify summer months (Ensuring CHARACTER format for raster matching)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# View(TwoLenBin200.dat)

# Try parsing both position 3 AND position 6, taking whichever works
TwoLenBin200_clean <- TwoLenBin200.dat %>%
  mutate(
    str_pos3 = str_split_fixed(keys, pattern = "_", 7)[, 3],
    str_pos6 = str_split_fixed(keys, pattern = "_", 7)[, 6],
    date_pos3 = parse_date_time(str_pos3, orders = c("ymd HMS"), quiet = TRUE),
    date_pos6 = parse_date_time(str_pos6, orders = c("ymd HMS"), quiet = TRUE),
    # Coalesce picks the first non-NA value (tries pos6 first, falls back to pos3)
    parsed_date = coalesce(date_pos6, date_pos3)
  )
# Extract your unique summer months as characters
months.list <- as.character(unique(month(TwoLenBin200_clean$parsed_date[!is.na(TwoLenBin200_clean$parsed_date)])))
print(months.list)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Convert unique grid centers to 10 km x 10 km polygons across all years
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Create sf object from spatial coordinates
grid_sf_centers <- st_as_sf(data_with_coords, 
                            coords = c("X", "Y"), 
                            crs = aea_custom,
                            remove = F) # Maintains centroid structure

# Optional: Add an explicit unique cell ID for bulletproof tracking
grid_sf_centers <- grid_sf_centers %>%
  mutate(cell_id = row_number())

# Replicate spatial points across years
grid_sf_df <- sdmTMB::replicate_df(
  grid_sf_centers, 
  "Year", 
  unique(TwoLenBin200.dat$Year)
)

# Re-assign sf class lost during replication and create 10km x 10km square buffers
grid_sf_polys <- grid_sf_df %>%
  st_as_sf(crs = aea_custom) %>%
  st_buffer(dist = 5000, endCapStyle = "SQUARE")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = grid_sf_polys, col = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18)

ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = data_with_coords, aes(x=X, y=Y)) +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. List ROMS NetCDF files
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fls <- list.files(
  here(dir, "Data", "ROMS2", "Regridded", "10x10km"), 
  pattern = "^allvars_mld_hindcast_.*\\_mld_masked_regrid.nc$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Extraction Function per Year
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_summer_mld <- function(f, all_polys, target_months) { 
  # Extract year from file name
  file_year <- as.numeric(regmatches(basename(f), regexpr("[0-9]{4}", basename(f))))
  
  # Filter grid polygons for THIS specific year
  year_polys <- all_polys %>% filter(Year == file_year)
  if (nrow(year_polys) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Load ROMS raster
  r <- terra::rast(f)
  
  # Sync names with month strings
  r_times <- terra::time(r)
  if (!all(is.na(r_times))) {
    names(r) <- as.character(as.numeric(format(r_times, "%m")))
  } else {
    names(r) <- as.character(1:12)
  }
  
  # Identify summer layers present (Character matching)
  avail_summer <- intersect(months.list, names(r))
  if (length(avail_summer) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Compute mean summer MLD layer
  r_summer_mean <- mean(r[[avail_summer]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Match CRS if needed
  if (st_crs(r_summer_mean) != st_crs(year_polys)) {
    r_summer_mean <- terra::project(r_summer_mean, crs(year_polys))
  }
  
  # Area-weighted extract onto 10km polygons
  mld_vals <- exactextractr::exact_extract(r_summer_mean, year_polys, 'mean', progress = FALSE)
  
  # Return tabular data with spatial join identifiers
  out <- year_polys %>%
    #st_drop_geometry() %>%
    mutate(
      mean_mld_m = mld_vals,
      source_file = basename(f)
    )
  
  return(out)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Parallel Execution
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

plan(multisession, workers = 6)

all_mld_results <- future_lapply(fls, function(f) {
  tryCatch(
    extract_summer_mld(f, grid_sf_polys, months.list),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
}, future.seed = TRUE)

plan(sequential)

# Combine into single table
mld_grid_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(all_mld_results)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Explore output
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Check results
head(mld_grid_table)

mean_mld_by_cell_by_year <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = mld_grid_table, aes(col = mean_mld_m)) +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
          color = "#ae8f60", 
          linewidth = 0.7, 
          fill = "#E1C699") +
```

# Finish creating prediction grid

```{r, finish.grid.creation}

# Replicate grid across years for summer
s2.grid.yr <- replicate_df(data_with_coords, ("Year"),
                           unique(TwoLenBin200.dat$Year))

# Replicate grid across merged.bins for summer
s2.grid.yr <- replicate_df(s2.grid.yr, ("merged.bin"),
                           unique(TwoLenBin200.dat$merged.bin))
                  
# Safely join MLD by X, Y, and Year
s2.grid.yr <- s2.grid.yr %>%
  left_join(
    mld_grid_table_final %>% 
      select(X, Y, Year, mean_mld_m), 
    by = c("X", "Y", "Year")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    YearSeas = paste0(Year,"Summer"),
    YearSeas.nm = as.numeric(paste0(Year,".1")),
    # Convert to km for prediction
    X = X/1000,
    # Convert to km for prediction
    Y = Y/1000,
    # Set offset to 0 for prediction grid, this will
    # allow for density to be predicted for every 
    # 1 unit effort in the model
    LogArea = 0,
    # Area of 10 km x 10 km grid cell in m^2
    cell_area_m2   = 100*1e6,
    # Calculate volume in m^3 for index integration
    cell_volume_m3_time_varyingMLD = cell_area_m2 * mean_mld_m,
    # Calculate volume in m^3 for index integration
    cell_volume_m3_time_mean_MLD = cell_area_m2 * mean(mean_mld_m, na.rm = T)
  )
                         
# 1. Close parallel workers so 100% of RAM is free for a single process
plan(sequential)

# 2. Force R to clean up unused memory
gc()

# 1. Filter out land cells where MLD or volume is NA / NaN
s2.grid.water <- s2.grid.yr %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(mean_mld_m), 
    !is.nan(mean_mld_m),
    !is.na(cell_volume_m3_time_varyingMLD),
    !is.nan(cell_volume_m3_time_varyingMLD),
    !is.na(cell_volume_m3_time_mean_MLD),
    !is.nan(cell_volume_m3_time_mean_MLD)
  ) %>%
  # 2. Also drop NAs for any other environmental covariates used in your model formula
  # e.g., filter(!is.na(depth), !is.na(temp)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Verify how many ocean cells remain vs total grid cells
cat("Original cells (with land):", nrow(s2.grid.yr), "\n")
cat("Water-only cells:", nrow(s2.grid.water), "\n")
cat("Remaining NAs:", sum(is.na(s2.grid.water$cell_volume_m3_time_varyingMLD)), "\n")

# Check visually
ggplot(s2.grid.water, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = mean_mld_m)) +
  geom_tile(width = 10, height = 10) + # Coordinates converted to km
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako",
    direction = -1,
    name = "MLD (m)") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Clean Ocean Prediction Grid (Land Masked Out)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18)

```

# Predict summer values onto grid with mean mld * area per year per cell

```{r, predict.on.grid_mean.mld.per.year.per.cell}

parallel::detectCores()

# Make predictions on the entire grid 
Summer.pred.no.imputations <- 
  predict(deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml, 
          newdata = s2.grid.water,
          offset  = s2.grid.water$LogArea,  # Manually supply the vector
          return_tmb_object = TRUE)

# Note unlike get_index_split() you use the prediction object and do not pass new data
index <- get_index(Summer.pred.no.imputations, 
                         bias_correct = TRUE, 
                         level = 0.95,
                         area = s2.grid.water$cell_volume_m3_time_varyingMLD
                         )

# Check if the maximum gradient is small (ideally < 0.001)
max(deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml$gradients)
# [1] 9.10719e-09        

# Check if the Hessian is positive definite
deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml$pos_def_hessian
# [1] TRUE

fwrite(index,  
       here(new_directory_path2,
            "deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml_index_MeanMLD-PerYearPerCell.10km.csv"),
       sep = ",")

```

```{r, adjust.units.for.projection}
  Summer.pred.no.imputations$data$X*1000

  Summer.pred.no.imputations$data$Y*1000


# Create the stars object directly from the data frame.
# 'stars' will automatically identify the unique X, Y, Year combinations
# and create a grid. All other numeric columns will become attributes.
Summer.pred_obj <- st_as_stars(Summer.pred.no.imputations$data,
                               dims = c("X", "Y", "Year", "merged.bin"))

# Specify the CRS for the stars object
```

# Try looping through Year Maps

## For fixed + random effects

For presence absence component 

```{r, year.lengthBin.map.est1.loop}

# Ensure the directory exists before the loop starts
if (!dir.exists(new_directory_path)) {
  dir.create(new_directory_path, recursive = TRUE)
}

# 1. Get the values for your loops
years <- attr(Summer.pred_obj, "dimensions")$Year$values$start
bins  <- attr(Summer.pred_obj, "dimensions")$merged.bin$values

# 2. Start the loops using numeric indices
for (y_idx in seq_along(years)) {
  current_year <- years[y_idx]
  
  for (b_idx in seq_along(bins)) {
    current_bin <- bins[b_idx]
    
    # SLICE THE STARS OBJECT: [attributes, X, Y, Year, Bin]
    # We leave the first 3 blank to get all variables and all space
    bin_subset <- Summer.pred_obj[, , , y_idx, b_idx]
    
    est.y1 <- ggplot() +
      # 1. Data Layer on top
      geom_stars(data = bin_subset, 
                 aes(fill = plogis(est1))) +
      # 2. Base Land Layers First
      geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
              color = "#ae8f60", 
              linewidth = 0.7, 
              fill = "#E1C699") +
      geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
              color = "#ae8f60", 
              linewidth = 0.7, 
              fill = "#E1C699") +
      ## To better visualize spatial patterns, the color scale for the 
      ## exponentiated predicted values 
      scale_fill_viridis_c(
        option = "inferno",
        direction = -1,
        limits = c(0, 1), # Fixed 0 to 1 scale for probability comparison across years
        labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
        guide = guide_colorbar(title = "Probability of\nOccurrence (0–1)")
        ) +
      ggtitle(paste("Summer Biomass - Year:", current_year, "\nBin:", current_bin, 
                    "- Fixed effects + all random effects")) +
      labs(y = "Latitude") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
      theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
            axis.text.x=element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x=element_blank())
    
    # FORCE PRINT for RMarkdown
    print(est.y1)
    
    # 3. Save Logic
    file_name <- paste0("BiomassMap_", current_year, "_", current_bin,
                        "FixedPlusRandom.effects.M1.jpg")
    full_destination <- file.path(new_directory_path, file_name)
    
    ggsave(
      filename = full_destination,
      plot = est.y1, 
      device = "jpeg", 
      dpi = 1200, 
      width = 45,      
      height = 21, 
      units = "cm", 
      limitsize = FALSE
      )
    
    # Optional: Clear the plot from memory to stay fast
    rm(est.y1)
    }
  }

```

## For random effects only

For presence absence component 

```{r, year.lengthBin.map.est_rf1.loop}

all_densities_est_rf1 <- Summer.pred_obj$est_rf1
min_dens_est_rf1 <- min(all_densities_est_rf1, na.rm = TRUE)
max_dens_est_rf1 <- max(all_densities_est_rf1, na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate the limit based ONLY on the data in this specific bin/year
# We use max(abs(...)) to ensure it is symmetric (e.g., -5.5 to 5.5)
current_range_est_rf1 <- range(bin_subset[["est_rf1"]], na.rm = TRUE)
dynamic_limit_est_rf1 <- max(abs(current_range_est_rf1))

# Debugging: Print this to your console so you can see it
print(paste("Data range is:", current_range_est_rf1[1], "to", current_range_est_rf1[2]))
print(paste("Setting limits to:", -dynamic_limit_est_rf1, "to", dynamic_limit_est_rf1))

# Optional: If your data has extreme outliers, you might want to 
# manually set the max to the 99th percentile to keep the maps readable.
# max_dens <- quantile(all_densities, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

# Ensure the directory exists before the loop starts
if (!dir.exists(new_directory_path)) {
  dir.create(new_directory_path, recursive = TRUE)
}

# 1. Get the values for your loops
years <- attr(Summer.pred_obj, "dimensions")$Year$values$start
bins  <- attr(Summer.pred_obj, "dimensions")$merged.bin$values

# 2. Start the loops using numeric indices
for (y_idx in seq_along(years)) {
  current_year <- years[y_idx]
  
  for (b_idx in seq_along(bins)) {
    current_bin <- bins[b_idx]
    
    # SLICE THE STARS OBJECT: [attributes, X, Y, Year, Bin]
    # We leave the first 3 blank to get all variables and all space
    bin_subset <- Summer.pred_obj[, , , y_idx, b_idx]
    
    est_rf.y1 <- ggplot() +
      # 1. Data Layer on top
      geom_stars(data = bin_subset, 
                 aes(fill = est_rf1)) +
      # 2. Base Land Layers First
      geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom,
              color = "#ae8f60", 
              linewidth = 0.7, 
              fill = "#E1C699") +
      geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
              color = "#ae8f60", 
              linewidth = 0.7, 
              fill = "#E1C699") +
      ## To better visualize spatial patterns, the color scale for the 
      ## exponentiated predicted values 
      scale_fill_gradient2(
        low = "blue",      # Color for negative effects (low biomass)
        mid = "white",     # Color for zero (neutral)
        high = "red",      # Color for positive effects (high biomass)
        midpoint = 0,      # CRITICAL: Fixes the neutral point at 0
        limits = c(-dynamic_limit_est_rf1, dynamic_limit_est_rf1), # Forces symmetry
        # THIS IS THE KEY:
        oob = scales::squish,
        na.value = "transparent",
        guide = guide_colorbar(title = "Random Effects\n(ω + ε)")
        ) +
      ggtitle(paste("Summer Biomass - Year:", current_year, "\nBin:", current_bin, 
                    "- Random effects")) +
      labs(y = "Latitude") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
      theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
            axis.text.x=element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x=element_blank())
    
    # FORCE PRINT for RMarkdown
    print(est_rf.y1)
    
    # 3. Save Logic
    file_name <- paste0("BiomassMap_", current_year, "_", current_bin, 
                        "random.effects.M1.jpg")
    full_destination <- file.path(new_directory_path, file_name)
    
    ggsave(
      filename = full_destination,
      plot = est_rf.y1, 
      device = "jpeg", 
      dpi = 1200, 
      width = 45,      
      height = 21, 
      units = "cm", 
      limitsize = FALSE
      )
    
    # Optional: Clear the plot from memory to stay fast
    rm(est_rf.y1)
    }
  }
```

```{r, year.lengthBin.map.omega_s1.loop}
              linewidth = 0.7, 
              fill = "#E1C699") +
      ## To better visualize spatial patterns, the color scale for the 
      ## exponentiated predicted values 
      scale_fill_gradient2(
        low = "blue",      # Color for negative effects (low biomass)
        mid = "white",     # Color for zero (neutral)
        high = "red",      # Color for positive effects (high biomass)
        midpoint = 0,      # CRITICAL: Fixes the neutral point at 0
        guide = guide_colorbar(title = "Spatial Random\nEffects (ω)")
        ) +
      ggtitle(paste("Summer Biomass - Year:", current_year, "\nBin:", current_bin, 
                    "- Sptl. Random effects")) +
      labs(y = "Latitude") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
      theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
            axis.text.x=element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x=element_blank())
    
    # FORCE PRINT for RMarkdown
    print(omega_s.y1)
    
    # 3. Save Logic
    file_name <- paste0("BiomassMap_", current_year, "_", current_bin,

    ggsave(

      width = 45,      
      height = 21, 
      units = "cm", 
      limitsize = FALSE
      )
    
    # Optional: Clear the plot from memory to stay fast
    rm(omega_s.y1)
    }
  }
}
```

```{r, year.lengthBin.map.omega_s2.loop}
bins  <- attr(Summer.pred_obj, "dimensions")$merged.bin$values

# 2. Start the loops using numeric indices
for (y_idx in seq_along(years)) {
```

```{r, year.lengthBin.map.zeta_s_merged.binless2001.loop}
      geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom,
              color = "#ae8f60", 
              linewidth = 0.7, 
              fill = "#E1C699") +
      ## To better visualize spatial patterns, the color scale for the 
      ## exponentiated predicted values 
      scale_fill_gradient2(
        low = "blue",      # Color for negative effects (low biomass)
        mid = "white",     # Color for zero (neutral)
        high = "red",      # Color for positive effects (high biomass)
        midpoint = 0,      # CRITICAL: Fixes the neutral point at 0
        # Use the dynamic limit we just calculated
        limits = c(-dynamic_limit_zeta_s_merged.binless2001,
                   dynamic_limit_zeta_s_merged.binless2001), 
        # THIS IS THE KEY:
        oob = scales::squish,
        na.value = "transparent",
        guide = 
          guide_colorbar(title = "Spatial Varying Coeff Effects\n(< 20.0 cm Length Bin (ζ))")
        ) +
      coord_sf() +

      labs(y = "Latitude") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
      theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
            axis.text.x=element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.x=element_blank())
    
    # FORCE PRINT for RMarkdown
    print(zeta_s_merged.binless200.y1)
    
    # 3. Save Logic
    file_name <- paste0("BiomassMap_", current_year, "_", current_bin,
```

# Run centre of gravity analysis by length bin

```{r, cog.analyses}

# Define covariate levels and years}
cov_levels <- c("less 20.0 cm", "20.0+ cm")
years <- sort(unique(s2.grid.water$Year))

cog.is.made = T

if (cog.is.made == F) {
  
cog_results <- list()

# Loop through each covariate level
for (lvl in cov_levels) {
  
  # Loop through each year to keep RAM usage low
  for (yr in years) {
    message("Calculating COG for Bin: ", lvl, " | Year: ", yr)
    
    # 1. Subset grid for THIS year AND set the specific covariate level
    grid_chunk <- s2.grid.water %>% 
      filter(Year == yr) %>% 
      mutate(merged.bin = lvl) %>%
      as.data.frame()
    
    # 2. Run predict on the SINGLE year chunk
    pred_obj <- predict(
      deltalognormalLogArea.sptlVarying3200Models.reml, 
      newdata = grid_chunk, 
      offset = grid_chunk$LogArea, # Vector length matches grid_chunk exactly
      return_tmb_object = TRUE
    )
    
    # 3. Calculate COG for this year/level chunk
    cog_chunk <- get_cog(
      pred_obj,
      bias_correct = TRUE, 
      level = 0.95,
      area = grid_chunk$cell_volume_m3_time_varyingMLD, # Vector matches grid_chunk
      format = "wide",
      silent = TRUE
    )
    
    # 4. Add identifying metadata columns
    cog_chunk$merged.bin <- lvl
    cog_chunk$Year <- yr
    
    # Store result in list
    cog_results[[paste(lvl, yr, sep = "_")]] <- cog_chunk
    
    # 5. PURGE RAM BEFORE NEXT ITERATION
    rm(pred_obj, grid_chunk, cog_chunk)
    gc(verbose = FALSE)
  }
}

# Stitch all chunks into one master data frame
final_cog <- bind_rows(cog_results)

# View final results
View(final_cog)

fwrite(final_cog, here(new_directory_path2, "centreofgravity.200mmLengthBins.csv"),
       sep = ",")

}

# Load data
final_cog <- fread( here(new_directory_path2, "centreofgravity.200mmLengthBins.csv"),
                    sep = ",")

NorthSouthMovement <-
  ggplot(final_cog, aes(x = Year, y = est_y, color = merged.bin, fill = merged.bin)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr_y, ymax = upr_y), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    y = "Northing COG (km)",
    title = "Northward/Southward Shift Over Time by Length Class"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18)

NorthSouthMovement

full_destination <- file.path(new_directory_path, "NorthSouthMovement.by200mmBin.jpg")

ggsave(
  filename = full_destination,
  plot = NorthSouthMovement, 
  device = "jpeg", 
  dpi = 1200, 
  width = 45,  
  height = 21,
  units = "cm", 
  limitsize = FALSE
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Calculate Map Bounding Box (Auto-Zoom to Trajectory)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create scaled coordinates in meters
cog_m <- final_cog %>% 
  mutate(x_m = est_x * 1000, y_m = est_y * 1000)

# Add a 50 km (50,000 m) buffer around your COG points
x_min <- min(cog_m$x_m, na.rm = TRUE) - 200000
x_max <- max(cog_m$x_m, na.rm = TRUE) + 200000
y_min <- min(cog_m$y_m, na.rm = TRUE) - 200000
y_max <- max(cog_m$y_m, na.rm = TRUE) + 200000

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Plot High-Contrast 2D Map
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

TwoDimensionalMovement <- ggplot() +
  
  # LAYER 1 & 2: LAND & STATES (Drawn FIRST in background)
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.5, fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.5, fill = "#E1C699") +
  
  # LAYER 3: BLACK PATH OUTLINE (Creates a sharp contrast halo)
  geom_path(
    data = cog_m, 
    aes(x = x_m, y = y_m, group = merged.bin), 
    color = "black", 
    linewidth = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  
  # LAYER 4: COLORED TRAJECTORY LINE & ARROW
  geom_path(
    data = cog_m, 
    aes(x = x_m, y = y_m, color = factor(Year), group = merged.bin), 
    linewidth = 0.9,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  
  # LAYER 5: CRISP BORDERED POINTS
  geom_point(
    data = cog_m, 
    aes(x = x_m, y = y_m, fill = factor(Year)), 
    shape = 21,       # Fillable circle with border
    color = "black",  # Black outer ring makes points pop
    size = 3.5,
    stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  
  # ZOOM MAP CLOSELY TO COG POINTS
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(x_min, x_max),
    ylim = c(y_min, y_max),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # FACETING AND COLORING
  facet_wrap(~merged.bin) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    name = "Year",
    breaks = c(2008, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019)
    ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    name = "Year",
    breaks = c(2008, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019)
    ) +
  
  # STYLING
  labs(
    x = "Longitude", 
    y = "Latitude",
    title = "2D Center of Gravity Trajectory Over Time",
    color = "Year",
    fill = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 90)
  )
```

# Create a single panel with all movement diagnostics

```{r, 2D-cog_vs_cog_vs_eao}

#-----------------------------------------
# For 2D centre of gravity map
#-----------------------------------------

# Create scaled coordinates in meters
cog_m <- final_cog %>% 
  mutate(x_m = est_x * 1000, y_m = est_y * 1000)

# Add a 50 km (50,000 m) buffer around your COG points
x_min <- min(cog_m$x_m, na.rm = TRUE) - 200000
x_max <- max(cog_m$x_m, na.rm = TRUE) + 200000
y_min <- min(cog_m$y_m, na.rm = TRUE) - 200000
y_max <- max(cog_m$y_m, na.rm = TRUE) + 200000

# Panel 0: High-Contrast 2D Map
p0 <- ggplot() +
  # LAYER 1 & 2: LAND & STATES (Drawn FIRST in background)
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.5, fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.5, fill = "#E1C699") +
  # LAYER 3: BLACK PATH OUTLINE (Creates a sharp contrast halo)
  geom_path(
    data = cog_m, 
    aes(x = x_m, y = y_m), 
    color = "black", 
    linewidth = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  # LAYER 4: COLORED TRAJECTORY LINE & ARROW
  geom_path(
    data = cog_m, 
    aes(x = x_m, y = y_m, color = factor(Year)), 
    linewidth = 0.9,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  # LAYER 5: CRISP BORDERED POINTS
  geom_point(
    data = cog_m, 
    aes(x = x_m, y = y_m, fill = factor(Year)), 
    shape = 21,       # Fillable circle with border
    color = "black",  # Black outer ring makes points pop
    size = 3.5,
    stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  # ZOOM MAP CLOSELY TO COG POINTS
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(x_min, x_max),
    ylim = c(y_min, y_max),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  # FACETING AND COLORING
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    name = "Year",
    breaks = c(2008, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019)
    ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    name = "Year",
    breaks = c(2008, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019)
    ) +
  # STYLING
  labs(
    x = "Longitude", 
    y = "Latitude",
    title = str_wrap("2D Center of Gravity Trajectory Over Time", width = 31),
    color = "Year",
    fill = "Year"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~merged.bin) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 90)
  )

#-----------------------------------------
# For North-South centre of gravity
#-----------------------------------------

# Prep COG Northing (Y coordinate)
cog_y <- final_cog %>% 
  select(Year, merged.bin, est_cog = est_y, lwr_cog = lwr_y, upr_cog = upr_y)

# Panel 1: Center of Gravity (Northing / Y)
p1 <- ggplot(cog_y, aes(x = Year, y = est_cog, color = merged.bin, fill = merged.bin)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr_cog, ymax = upr_cog), alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2008, 2019, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right") + # Move Y-axis to the right
  labs(y = "Northing COG (km)", title = "Spatial Centroid Shift (COG)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        plot.margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0, unit = "pt"))

#-----------------------------------------
# For Effective volume occupied 
#-----------------------------------------

# Prep EVO
evo_clean <- final_eao %>% 
  select(Year, merged.bin, est_evo = est, lwr_evo = lwr, upr_evo = upr)

# Panel 2: Effective Volume Occupied (EvO)
p2 <- ggplot(evo_clean, aes(x = Year, y = est_evo, color = merged.bin, fill = merged.bin)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr_evo, ymax = upr_evo), alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2008, 2019, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right") + # Move Y-axis to the right
  labs(y = "Occupied Volume (m³)", title = "Effective Volume Footprint (EVO)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0, unit = "pt"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combine Plots & Format for CJFAS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Attach legend to p0 and strip panel margins
p0_tight <- p0 + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "left",
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), 
    plot.margin = margin(t = 0, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0, unit = "pt")
  )

p0_tight

# 2. Combine northward cog and evo into a clean single column layout
temp_fig <- p1 / p2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect") 

temp_fig

# 3. Combine everything into a clean 2-column layout
final_fig <- p0_tight + temp_fig +
  plot_layout(widths = c(0.55, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = 'a',
    tag_prefix = '(',
    tag_suffix = ')'
  ) & 
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), 
    plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1, "pt") # Minimal padding around panels
  ) & 
  labs(title = NULL)

final_fig

full_destination <- file.path(new_directory_path, "2DGOGvsCOGvsEVO.200LengthBin.jpg")

ggsave(
  filename = full_destination,
  plot = final_fig, 
  device = "jpeg", 
  dpi = 1200, 
  width = 45,     
  height = 21, 
  units = "cm", 
  limitsize = FALSE
  )

```

# For write up, identify direction of EVO trend and check which years are significant

Woillez et al. (2007; 2009)
Citation: Woillez, M., et al. (2007). 
Notes on aggregation indices for spatial distributions of fish populations. ICES Journal of Marine Science, 64(9), 1837–1841.
Role: Establishes the foundational use of *CV* across time series of spatial indices (e.g., Area Occupied, Center of Gravity) to quantify population spatial stability versus environmental responsiveness.

Thorson et al. (2016)
Citation: Thorson, J. T., et al. (2016). 
Model-based inference for estimating shifts in species distribution, area occupied and centre of gravity. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7(8), 990–1002.
Role: Demonstrates evaluating interannual variance and relative fluctuation (*CV*) in model-based effective area/volume occupied across climate anomalies.

Ciannelli et al. (2013)
Citation: Ciannelli, L., et al. (2013). Spatial convergence and divergence in fish distributions. Ecography, 36(1), 108–118.
Role: Uses *CV* of spatial indices to measure dynamic range expansion/contraction under density-dependent habitat selection.

```{r, eao.analyses.additional.stats}

# For understanding baseline and percent changes (gives direction)
final_eao_summary <- final_eao %>%
  group_by(merged.bin) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline = mean(est),
    pct_change = ((est - baseline) / baseline) * 100,
    pct_lwr    = ((lwr - baseline) / baseline) * 100,
    pct_upr    = ((upr - baseline) / baseline) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

View(final_eao_summary)

fwrite(final_eao_summary, here(new_directory_path2, "effectiveareaoccupied.200mmLengthBins_summary.csv"),
       sep = ",")

# Because the above pattern is so chaotic, see if there is any meaning here
## For volatility by size
cv_by_bin <- final_eao %>%
  group_by(merged.bin) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_evo = mean(est),
    sd_evo   = sd(est),
    cv_evo   = (sd_evo / mean_evo) * 100
  )

View(cv_by_bin)

fwrite(cv_by_bin, here(new_directory_path2, "cv_by_bin.csv"),
       sep = ",")

## For volatility by size and blob event
cv_by_regime <- final_eao %>%
  mutate(
    regime = case_when(
      Year < 2014 ~ "Pre-Blob",
      Year %in% 2014:2016 ~ "Blob",
      Year > 2016 ~ "Post-Blob"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(merged.bin, regime) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_evo = mean(est),
    sd_evo   = sd(est),
    cv_evo   = (sd_evo / mean_evo) * 100,
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

View(cv_by_regime)

fwrite(cv_by_regime, here(new_directory_path2, "cv_by_regime.csv"),
       sep = ",")

```

```{r}

# 1. Calculate a unified symmetric limit across BOTH datasets
combined_vals <- c(
  bin_subset[["zeta_s_merged.binless 20.0 cm1"]],
  bin_subset[["zeta_s_merged.binless 20.0 cm2"]]
)
shared_limit <- max(abs(combined_vals), na.rm = TRUE)

# 2. Define a single reusable scale object
shared_fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient2(
  low = "blue",      
  mid = "white",     
  high = "red",     
  midpoint = 0,      
  limits = c(-shared_limit, shared_limit), 
  # Expands resolution near 0; sigma controls how close to 0 the expansion starts
  transform = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.1),
  oob = scales::squish,
  na.value = "transparent",
  guide = guide_colorbar(
    title = "Spatial Varying\nCoeff Effects\n< 20.0 cm (ζ)"
  )
)


# 3. Build Plot 1
zeta_plot.presence <- ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = Summer.pred_obj, aes(fill = `zeta_s_merged.binless 20.0 cm1`)) +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.7, fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.7, fill = "#E1C699") +
  shared_fill_scale +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(y = "Latitude") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

# 4. Build Plot 2
zeta_plot.posCatch <- ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = Summer.pred_obj, aes(fill = `zeta_s_merged.binless 20.0 cm2`)) +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.7, fill = "#E1C699") +
  geom_sf(data = PCoastStates.aea_custom, color = "#ae8f60", linewidth = 0.7, fill = "#E1C699") +
  shared_fill_scale +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

# 5. Combine plots with collected guide
```
